question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (Channelized intersection) of Figure 2A-3, no dimension is given from the nose of the island to the YIELD sign. The YIELD sign is shown placed on the right-hand roadside of the channelized approach with a lateral offset of "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." from the edge of the roadway; the only sign associated with the island itself is dimensioned with "2 ft MIN." clearance from the island's edges. The evidence therefore does not support a specific nose-of-island distance for the YIELD sign. Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." (This corresponds to the 2 ft MIN. clearance dimension shown for the island-mounted sign in Drawing B, not for the YIELD sign.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B (Channelized intersection), shows the YIELD sign on the right side of the channelized approach with a "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the pavement edge, and a separate sign on the channelizing island with "2 ft MIN." clearances from the island edges — no dimension is shown from the island nose to the YIELD sign. [Image 4] shows the same Figure 2A-3 in the page context (p.52), confirming the same dimensions and the figure note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989)
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
